   "id": "09118d7a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Bivariate data - Models"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "840c0733",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "This tutorial focuses on fitting simple regression models to bivariate data using `plans`, and assessing them with the model panel and fit metrics.\n",
    "\n",
    "```{seealso}\n",
    "Check out the {doc}`Bivariate data - Basics <bivar_01>` tutorial first.\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "46dad7a5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Notebook setup\n",
    "\n",
    "For users running this tutorial as a Jupyter Notebook, this cell must be executed first:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "8bed0e4e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.310257Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.309815Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.756463Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.755851Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Outputs will be saved to: ./outputs\\bivariate\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import sys\n",
    "from pathlib import Path\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "# Install `plans` in `google.colab`.\n",
    "# Use `pip install plans` for other environments.\n",
    "\n",
    "if \"google.colab\" in sys.modules:\n",
    "    import os\n",
    "    os.system(f\"{sys.executable} -m pip install -q plans\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# This avoids warnings related to uninstalled fonts\n",
    "import logging\n",
    "# Set the matplotlib font manager logger to only show errors (hides warnings)\n",
    "logging.getLogger('matplotlib.font_manager').setLevel(logging.ERROR)\n",
    "\n",
    "# define output folder\n",
    "OUTPUT_DIR = Path(\"outputs/bivariate\")\n",
    "OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n",
    "print(f\"Outputs will be saved to: ./{OUTPUT_DIR}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "014822c0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Create synthetic rating curve\n",
    "\n",
    "Stage-discharge relations (rating curves) are a classic case for model fitting in hydrology. Discharge usually starts at a stage offset (the gauge zero is below the channel bottom), so lets make one with $h_0 = 0.2$ m plus gaussian noise. Stages are drawn from a skewed (gamma) distribution, since low flows are far more frequent than floods in a real gauging record:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "0396d96a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.760291Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T22:23:12.759860Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.356751Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.355891Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 478.346x472.441 with 3 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from plans.datasets.analyst import Bivar\n",
    "\n",
    "# make synthetic power-law data with a stage offset\n",
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)  # ensure reproducibility\n",
    "h = 0.3 + rng.gamma(shape=1.5, scale=0.4, size=200)  # skewed to low stages\n",
    "q = 5 * np.power(h - 0.2, 1.6) + rng.normal(loc=0, scale=0.5, size=len(h))\n",
    "\n",
    "bv = Bivar(name=\"Rating Curve\", alias=\"RC\")\n",
    "bv.xname = \"Stage\"\n",
    "bv.xunits = \"m\"\n",
    "bv.yname = \"Discharge\"\n",
    "bv.yunits = \"m3/s\"\n",
    "bv.set_data(x=h, y=q)\n",
    "bv.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "27fa1866",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Available models"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "10acbdc2",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Models are stored in the `.models` dictionary. Each entry holds the function, its formula, a `Setup` table of parameters (initial guesses before fitting) and, once computed, the model `Data` and `Metrics`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "ca2bee0f",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.359743Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.359261Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.364743Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T22:23:13.363896Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Linear       f(x) = c0 + c1 * x\n",
      "Power        f(x) =  c2 * ((x + c0)^c1)\n",
      "Power_zero   f(x) =  c1 * (x^c0)\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "for model_type, model in bv.models.items():\n",
    "    print(f\"{model_type:<12} {model['Formula']}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fd43df5f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Fitting models\n",
    "\n",
    "The `.fit()` method runs a least squares fit and stores the mean and standard deviation of parameters in the `Setup` table. The `model` layout shows the fitted curve, how the error variance evolves along `x`, the errors, their histogram and a Q-Q plot against the normal distribution."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "aab46a71",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fc31eb8c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Note that $\\rho$ is the same for all models: they are all increasing curves, so they rank the predictions in the same order. Here $r$, $R^2$ and the errors are what separate the models. Also, $R^2$ equals $r^2$ only for the least-squares linear model:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "id": "88247e1b",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T22:23:16.614462Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T22:23:16.610894Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T22:23:16.629990Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T22:23:16.628335Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Linear R2: 0.9271\n",
      "Linear r^2: 0.9271\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "print(f\"Linear R2: {df_metrics.loc['Linear', 'R2']:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Linear r^2: {df_metrics.loc['Linear', 'r'] ** 2:.4f}\")"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "ls_dfs = []\n",
    "for model_type in bv.models:\n",
    "    df = bv.get_error_normality(model_type=model_type, clevel=0.95)\n",
    "    df.insert(0, \"Model\", model_type)\n",
    "    ls_dfs.append(df)\n",
    "pd.concat(ls_dfs, ignore_index=True)"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## Set parameters manually\n",
    "\n",
    "Parameters can also be set by hand with `.update_model()`, for instance to test a known reference curve. Metrics and the model data are updated accordingly:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 17,
   "id": "c444a524",
